summary.text: A 59-year-old woman was referred to a tertiary clinic with increased thyroglobulin during follow-up of follicular thyroid carcinoma diagnosed nine years earlier (pT2N0) and treated with total thyroidectomy and 30 mCi of I-131. The post-ablation iodine scan showed no pathologic finding apart from a post surgical thyroid remnant, and her first serum Tg was 0.01 ng/mL with absent anti-Tg antibody.

She had poorly adhered to follow-up. An empirical 200 mCi I-131 dose was given with a negative post-treatment scan. At a follow-up, Tg was more than 500 ng/mL with suppressed TSH, and neck ultrasonography and a diagnostic I-131 scan were negative. Rising serum Tg above 30,000 ng/mL without anti-Tg antibody was documented, and she reported severe sternal pain. FDG PET/CT showed pulmonary nodules and a lytic sternal manubrium lesion, and Ga-68 DOTA-TATE PET/CT showed the lesions with high somatostatin receptor density; the order of the two scans differs between abstract and case text. lu177 DOTA-TATE therapy was planned.

She received 200 mci of lu177 DOTA-TATE, and post-treatment SPECT/CT showed uptake in the pulmonary nodules and the margin of the sternal lytic lesion. Tg declined to 1,760 ng/mL three months after the first cycle and to 982 ng/mL two months after the second cycle, and after two cycles she reported that her sternal pain and dyspnea were much better.
